---
title: "gt Integration"
---

Gridwell integrates with [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com/) to render gt table objects to all 11
output formats from R.

## Quick Start

```r
library(gt)
library(gridwell)

tbl <- gt(exibble, rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") |>
  tab_header(title = "Example", subtitle = "From exibble")

html <- gw_render_html(tbl)
```

Every gridwell function takes a gt table and converts it on the way in. To convert
once, use `as_gw_table()`, which gives a `gw_table`:

```r
gw <- as_gw_table(tbl)
gw                    # <gw_table: 8 columns, 8 rows in 2 groups, titled "Example">
                      # and the table drawn as text
```

In R Markdown and Quarto, a `gw_table` a chunk returns is shown as the document's
format: HTML (with styles scoped to that table, and marked so Quarto doesn't add
Bootstrap's table styling), LaTeX for PDF (asking for the LaTeX packages it uses), or
Typst. Word and PowerPoint documents get the table drawn as text; to put a real table
in one, save it with `gw_save(tbl, "table.docx")`.

## Functions

### `as_gw_table(x)`

A `gw_table` from a gt table, IR as a JSON string, or a `gw_table` (returned as is).

### `gt_to_ir(gt_tbl, emitter = "auto")`

Converts a `gt_tbl` object to gridwell IR JSON string.

```r
ir_json <- gt_to_ir(tbl)
```

### `gt_to_ir_list(gt_tbl, emitter = "auto")`

Converts a `gt_tbl` object to an R list (IR structure).

```r
ir_list <- gt_to_ir_list(tbl)
```

### Which converter

The converter is moving into gt, as `gt::as_ir()`, since it reads gt's internals and
gt can keep it in step with them. Until every gt has it, gridwell keeps its own copy.
`emitter` picks one:

- `"auto"` (the default): gt's when the installed gt has `as_ir()`, and gridwell's
  otherwise. If gt's fails, or gives an IR major version this gridwell can't read,
  gridwell's is used with a warning saying why.
- `"upstream"`: gt's, with an error if there is none or it can't be used.
- `"gridwell"`: gridwell's.

No released gt has `as_ir()` yet, so today `"auto"` always uses gridwell's.

## What Gets Converted

| gt Feature | IR Mapping |
|------------|-----------|
| Column labels (`_boxhead`) | `thead` rows |
| Row groups (`_row_groups`) | `tbody` array with group labels |
| Stub column (`rowname_col`) | Cells with `is_stub: true`, always aligned left |
| A stub of several columns (`rowname_col = c("region", "city")`) | One stub column each, outermost first; consecutive rows of a group with the same outer value (and the same values to its left) share one cell spanning them, merged in the order the rows are shown |
| Row group column (`row_group_as_column = TRUE`) | The first stub column: each group's label is a stub cell spanning its rows, and the group has no label row. A summary row's label spans the other stub columns, beside an empty cell under the group's label (gt's HTML has the group's cell span its summary rows instead) |
| Stubhead label (`tab_stubhead()`) | One head cell spanning the stub columns; a vector of labels gives each row stub column its own, with a blank one above a row group column |
| Title/subtitle (`_heading`) | `header` block |
| Summary rows (`summary_rows()`, `grand_summary_rows()`) | A group's `summary_rows`, and a last group without a label for the grand summary. A group whose summary rows are all on its top side (`side = "top"`) has them at the top (`summary_placement: "top"`); one with rows on both sides has them all at the bottom. A grand summary on the top side is a first group without a label, with its rows at the top |
| Table id (`gt(id =)`) | `config.id`, which the HTML writer uses as its `table_id` when that option isn't set; an id that isn't an HTML id (empty, or with whitespace) is left out |
| Border options (`tab_options(table.border.top.color = …)` and the like) | The table's [rules](../schema/config.qmd#rules), where changed from gt's defaults, as the [Great Tables guide](integration-great-tables.qmd#borders) describes for the same options; styles the IR has no rule for (`groove` and the like) are left out |
| Source notes (`_source_notes`) | `footer.source_notes` |
| Column alignment | `column_spec[].align` |
| Column widths | `column_spec[].width` |
| Data values | Cell `content` and `typed_value` |
| Typed values | The number displayed, read as the Python package reads it (in any locale's marks; without its currency or unit; `0.451` for `45.1%`; scaled for scientific and compact notation; none for a display that isn't one number, such as `<0.001`). `POSIXct` date-times are typed as their wall-clock time in their own time zone, and `hms` times of day as times |

## Full Pipeline Example

```r
library(gt)
library(gridwell)

tbl <- gt(exibble, rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group") |>
  tab_header(title = "Example", subtitle = "Demo") |>
  tab_source_note(source_note = "Source: gt package")

gw <- as_gw_table(tbl)

# Validate
errors <- gw_validate(gw)
stopifnot(length(errors) == 0)

# Text formats
for (fmt in c("html", "latex", "typst", "rtf", "svg", "ansi", "pandoc", "quarto")) {
  result <- gw_render(gw, fmt)
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d chars\n", fmt, nchar(result)))
}

# Binary formats
for (fmt in c("docx", "xlsx", "pptx")) {
  data <- gw_render_binary(gw, fmt)
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d bytes\n", fmt, length(data)))
}
```
